bullets.title: Korea KOSPI -10% triggers global semi selloff; levered ETF structure amplifying moves
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI crashed ~10%, with SK Hynix and Samsung each down >12%, triggering a circuit breaker for the fourth time this year. Korean retail margin loans hit a record $26B and leveraged single-stock ETFs (hastily approved per the regulator) amplified the volatility. The selloff spread to US markets with SOX implying a ~12% decline and NDX futures down 2.4-2.6%, though multiple desks characterize this as a positioning/crowded-trade unwind rather than a fundamental AI memory thesis break.

bullets.title: MU earnings Wednesday are the pivotal AI catalyst; buyside consensus bullish on SCAs and margins
bullets.body: Micron reports F3Q26 Wednesday after close with Street expecting $19.77B revenue, 81.2% gross margin, and $20.83 EPS — all above guidance midpoints. ~75% of surveyed buyside investors expect new Strategic Customer Agreements announcements, MU-Anthropic deal already announced. Options are pricing the largest implied move (+10%) in a decade; 75% of Citi survey respondents expect MU above $1,000 post-print. Key watch items: LTAs, agentic AI commentary, and the August quarter guide which could reset memory cycle expectations.

bullets.title: Fed 'bang-bang' policy shift under Warsh driving front-end rate pressure; markets pricing 50bp of hikes by March 2027
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh is moving away from gradualism toward meeting-by-meeting decisions, with markets now pricing 9-10bps of July hikes and 50bp total by March 2027. JPMorgan flagged hawkish upcoming Fed speakers (Williams, Goolsbee, Barkin) and noted bond fund positioning is nearly two standard deviations shorter than the 1-year average. Goolsbee separately warned services inflation is 'disturbing' and trending the wrong way, while Core Services YoY has increased three consecutive months.

bullets.title: AI trade faces multiple headwinds: open-source competition, talent departures, ROI scrutiny, token deflation
bullets.body: GOOGL fell 5% on DeepMind VP departures to Anthropic and reports that China's GLM-5.2 matches Gemini 3 Pro on SWE-bench at a fraction of the cost. Goldman notes AI race is shifting from frontier labs to model orchestration/open-source, accelerating token deflation and pressuring model economics. Trump administration also barred foreign access to Anthropic advanced platforms, pushing some users toward Chinese AI alternatives. Hyperscalers remain structural capex winners but first to show equivalent output at lower spend will be rewarded.

bullets.title: Semis/Software bifurcation extreme: SOX +116% YTD vs IGV -17.6%; rotation risk rising
bullets.body: The semiconductor ETF (SMH) is up 86-116% YTD while software (IGV) is down ~17.6% YTD, creating one of the most bifurcated tech tape setups in years. Hedge funds net sold US equities at ~3 standard deviations, concentrating shorts in Software (-3std) and Autos (-2.3std). Retail has net sold semis ($68M outflows) while institutional money continues flowing to NVDA, AVGO, and TSM. Multiple desks note gross HF leverage peaked unusually high around mid-June expiry, historically leading to larger-than-average post-expiry declines (~5% avg).

bullets.title: Russell rebalance Friday June 26 creates significant semi flows: MU +$8B inflow, AAPL -$9B shift
bullets.body: Russell rebalance effective June 26 drives notable mechanical flows: MU moving from 100% value to 100% growth (+$8B inflow), AAPL shifting from 100% growth to 55% growth/45% value (-$9.1B). NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TXN also see inflows; CRDO and FN see outflows. SPCX is the largest add at $3.4B net flow; FN the largest promotion remove at -$2.2B.

bullets.title: JPMorgan estimates ~$165B equity-selling/bond-buying rebalancing flow from month/quarter-end
bullets.body: JPMorgan estimated approximately $165B of price-insensitive equity selling paired with bond buying from month- and quarter-end rebalancing, adding to near-term market pressure. Separately, Wells Fargo noted $28B in tariff refunds already issued since May with potential $66B net benefit in 2H, and estimated $20B of price-insensitive inflows from Trump accounts starting in July — a partial offset.

bullets.title: US-Iran deal: oil falling from $120+ to high-$70s; ECB consistent with one more hike in September
bullets.body: Brent crude has collapsed from >$120/bbl to the high-$70s following Hormuz reopening and a 60-day US temporary general license for Iranian crude. Morgan Stanley forecasts $90/bbl for 3Q26 and sees the deal as near-term positive for US equities via lower inflation. Meanwhile, ECB's Lagarde and Lane comments are consistent with a final hike in September; eurozone ex-Ireland PMI signals 0.6% annualized 2Q growth. Euro area composite PMI rose 0.9pt to 49.5 in June, partially reflecting Iran ceasefire relief.

bullets.title: Goldman's GIR: AI market gains now exceed baseline PDV of capex; requires more optimistic adoption assumptions
bullets.body: Goldman's GIR analysis finds that AI-driven equity market gains now exceed baseline estimates of the present discounted value of AI capex, meaning current valuations require more optimistic adoption and productivity assumptions. JPMorgan maintains $5.5T AI capex estimate through 2030 but sees better near-term risk/reward in Japan SPEs and China AI plays versus memory. Liquid cooling basket (ECL, MOD, DOV, ETN, JCI) has outperformed Mag 7 by 13.5% since mid-May as infrastructure-layer picks gain traction.

bullets.title: Trump signs Quantum Innovation EO; QCOM eyeing $4B Modular acquisition
bullets.body: Trump signed executive orders to accelerate quantum research for federal cyber defense, with administration targeting a functional quantum computer by 2028. The EO provided a catalyst for quantum-linked names (QBTS +2.9%). Separately, Qualcomm is in advanced talks to acquire AI infrastructure software firm Modular for ~$4B, signaling the company's pivot toward AI chip software stacks.

bullets.title: PCE preview: Goldman sees Core PCE 3.2% by Dec 2026, easing to 2.2% by Dec 2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs forecasts Core PCE inflation at 3.2% by December 2026, slowing to 2.2% by December 2027 as AI efficiency gains and energy effects fade. JPMorgan expects core PCE in line with consensus at 0.3% MoM for the upcoming print. Wolfe Research forecasts June nonfarm payrolls at 155K (vs 118K consensus), with a 35K boost from World Cup hiring in leisure/hospitality; sees 0.26% MoM AHE growth.

bullets.title: Eurozone and UK PMIs: Euro area recovering on Iran deal; UK at 49.4 with sticky inflation
bullets.body: Euro area June composite PMI rose to 49.5 (from ~48.6) with demand, employment, and sentiment all strengthening, though most responses predate the mid-June Iran deal so the final reading may be revised higher. UK composite PMI fell to 49.4, consistent with 0.2% annualized GDP growth, as services dropped to 48.7 on consumer confidence weakness; output prices remain elevated at 60.1, well above pre-war levels.

bullets.title: S&P 500 seasonality: weak June historically but July averages +3.37% with 100% hit rate
bullets.body: JPMorgan notes June seasonality is weak in the last two weeks, but July is historically very strong with a 100% hit rate and average return of +3.37%. For the full year, the S&P is up ~5% in 1H; historically when 1H returns exceed 5%, 2H averages +7% versus +2.5% otherwise. CTA exposure sits at only the 24th percentile with significant room to re-lever if realized volatility declines.

bullets.title: Memory fundamentals intact despite Korea selloff; SK Hynix shifting capacity from HBM4 to commodity DRAM
bullets.body: SK Hynix is modestly slowing HBM4 ramp and reallocating capacity to commodity DRAM where margins exceed HBM by 15+ percentage points. Samsung HBM4 revenue surpassed $1B in just four months from production start. DRAM spot pricing is up 52% since January and 22% since April. Multiple desks characterize the KOSPI crash as an overcrowded-trade cleanup rather than a fundamental shift in the AI memory thesis, though Nvidia Rubin certification remains in progress per SK Hynix.

bullets.title: Software IGV down sharply YTD; infrastructure software more resilient than pure SaaS
bullets.body: IGV is down ~15.7% YTD versus S&P 500 +10.1%, with all-SaaS index trading at only 4.9x FY+2 EV/Sales. Software is being sold indiscriminately, though infrastructure names like PANW and CRWD are more resilient. NFLX dropped to ~20x NTM P/E (4-year lows) amid meta's Instagram TV expansion and YouTube gaining watch-time share (99 min/day vs NFLX's 93). US software shorts are being re-laid at -1.7 standard deviations after spring covering.

bullets.title: Bending Spoons (BSP) IPO pricing June 30 at $26-28; $1.6B deal via Goldman/JPM
bullets.body: Bending Spoons S.p.A. is pricing its NASDAQ IPO on June 30, 2026 at $26-28/share for ~58M shares (59% primary, 41% secondary), implying ~$1.565B deal size with a 15% greenshoe. The company's portfolio includes Vimeo, Eventbrite, Evernote, WeTransfer, and AOL, serving 500M+ MAUs and 9M+ monthly paying customers. Bookrunners are Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Allen & Co.

bullets.title: Antitrust: federal enforcement risk declining; META clearest beneficiary, GOOGL/AMZN face behavioral not structural remedies
bullets.body: Mizuho's antitrust expert call concludes federal tech antitrust enforcement risk is declining as FTC leadership gaps and anti-big-tech hawks depart, with the FTC likely to become an arm of the administration. Courts consistently decline structural remedies in favor of behavioral ones; META faces negligible breakup risk after winning at trial on market definition. GOOGL's liability finding is credibly reversible on appeal; AMZN's case is furthest from resolution and most binary.

bullets.title: ACN managed services bookings -15% YoY signals AI crowding out IT spend; PT cut across multiple banks
bullets.body: Accenture's F3Q26 managed services bookings declined 15% YoY versus investor expectations of +4-5%, with consulting growing +11% CC y/y offsetting the decline. Morgan Stanley cut PT to $130 from $177, flagging the weakness may reflect AI displacing traditional IT spend rather than project pushouts. Mizuho cut PT to $226 from $280. ACN simultaneously raised FY26 buyback by $2B to $7.5B total (62% YoY increase), all to be completed by August 31.

bullets.title: AMZN Prime Day (Jun 23-26) expected to shift $7-8B incremental revenue into Q2; 370M+ subs by year-end
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Prime deep dive estimates the service delivers ~$1,440/year in value against a $139 cost; Prime Day is a 4-day event this year expected to shift $7-8B of global incremental revenue into Q2 with 6% Y/Y growth in 3P and 7% in 1P sales. Amazon projects 370M+ Prime subscribers by year-end (139M US, 231M international). A $20 price increase — now more likely in 2027 than 2026 due to macro — could drive ~$3B in incremental annualized net sales. JPM maintains AMZN as Best Idea with $330 PT.

bullets.title: Oil bias lower but execution risk remains; supply normalization must outpace demand for sustained downside
bullets.body: The first phase of war-premium removal is largely complete with Brent moving from $120+ to the high-$70s. Iran is returning barrels through formal channels while Gulf producers (Kuwait, Iraq, UAE) ramp output rapidly. OPEC+ is adding supply and SPR has 35-40Mb remaining. However, physical normalization is incomplete — shipping conditions remain complex, insurance/sanctions frictions persist, and refinery utilization near ~97% caps incremental demand absorption. Directional bias is lower but sustained downside requires proof supply normalization outpaces demand.
